edges.description: MECP2 coding, regulatory, and 3'-UTR variation reduces or destabilizes functional MeCP2 in neurons.
Reduced or dysregulated MeCP2 alters its methyl-CpG-dependent transcriptional control of neuronal target genes.
Altered MeCP2-dependent transcription disrupts activity-dependent synapse development and neuronal maturation.
Disrupted synaptic maturation and circuit E/I balance manifest as core autistic behavior.

nodes.description: Core autism spectrum phenotype — persistent deficits in social communication and interaction with restricted, repetitive behavior — is the defining manifestation that MECP2 variation predisposes toward in AUTSX3.

evidence.reference_title: Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 polymorphisms and vulnerability to autism.
evidence.snippet: This suggests that one or more functional variants of MECP2 existing at significant frequencies in the population may confer increased risk of autism/autism spectrum disorders

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 structural and 3'-UTR variants in schizophrenia, autism and other psychiatric diseases: a possible association with autism.
evidence.snippet: These mutations suggest that a possible association between MECP2 mutations and autism may warrant further study.

nodes.description: MeCP2 binds methylated CpG dinucleotides and functions as both a transcriptional repressor (via histone deacetylase/SIN3A corepressor complexes) and an activator, regulating a wide range of neuronal genes. Partial loss or dysregulation of MeCP2 shifts these activity-dependent gene-expression programs, providing the molecular bridge from MECP2 variation to altered neuronal maturation.

evidence.reference_title: Rett syndrome is caused by mutations in X-linked MECP2, encoding methyl-CpG-binding protein 2.
evidence.snippet: MeCP2 selectively binds CpG dinucleotides in the mammalian genome and mediates transcriptional repression through interaction with histone deacetylase and the corepressor SIN3A

evidence.reference_title: Transcriptional repression by the methyl-CpG-binding protein MeCP2 involves a histone deacetylase complex.
evidence.snippet: We show that a region of MeCP2 that localizes with the TRD associates with a corepressor complex containing the transcriptional repressor mSin3A and histone deacetylases.

evidence.reference_title: MeCP2, a key contributor to neurological disease, activates and represses transcription.
evidence.snippet: These studies suggest that MeCP2 regulates the expression of a wide range of genes in the hypothalamus and that it can function as both an activator and a repressor of transcription.

nodes.description: Convergent dysregulation of MeCP2-dependent gene expression impairs activity-dependent synaptic maturation and, in model systems, the function of GABAergic (inhibitory) neurons — perturbing the excitatory/inhibitory balance of developing cortical circuits. Mouse studies deleting Mecp2 from GABAergic neurons recapitulate autistic and Rett-like features, providing a mechanistic link (in animal models) from MeCP2 dosage sensitivity to autistic behavior, intellectual disability, and language impairment across the MECP2 spectrum.

evidence.reference_title: Reduced MeCP2 expression is frequent in autism frontal cortex and correlates with aberrant MECP2 promoter methylation.
evidence.snippet: These results suggest that both genetic and epigenetic defects lead to reduced MeCP2 expression and may be important in the complex etiology of autism.

evidence.reference_title: Dysfunction in GABA signalling mediates autism-like stereotypies and Rett syndrome phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: These data demonstrate that MeCP2 is critical for normal function of GABA-releasing neurons and that subtle dysfunction of GABAergic neurons contributes to numerous neuropsychiatric phenotypes.

evidence.reference_title: Methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 polymorphisms and vulnerability to autism.
evidence.snippet: has provided evidence for significant association (P = 0.009) for a three-marker SNP haplotype of MECP2 with autism/autism spectrum disorders

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
evidence.snippet: Our results suggest that MECP2 can play a role in autism etiology, although very rarely, supporting the notion that MECP2 mutations underlie several neurodevelopmental disorders.

nodes.description: The AUTSX3 susceptibility is anchored on variation at the X-linked MECP2 gene that falls short of the classic Rett-causing loss-of-function threshold: rare de novo mutations in autistic females, a non-lethal missense change in an autistic male, and an excess of conserved 3'-UTR variants that alter transcript stability. These alleles broaden the MECP2 phenotypic spectrum beyond Rett syndrome and severe neonatal encephalopathy toward autism.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of MeCP2 mutations in a series of females with autistic disorder.
evidence.snippet: Two autistic disorder females were found to have de novo mutations in the MeCP2 gene.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 structural and 3'-UTR variants in schizophrenia, autism and other psychiatric diseases: a possible association with autism.
evidence.snippet: A higher frequency of missense and 3'-UTR variants was found in autism.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
evidence.snippet: The novel missense change, c.617G > C (p.G206A), was present in one autistic male with severe mental retardation and absence of language, and segregates in his maternal family.

nodes.description: Neuronal MeCP2 abundance is tightly regulated, and autism brain frequently shows reduced MeCP2 expression. Conserved 3'-UTR variants lower MECP2 mRNA levels, and increased MECP2 promoter methylation in male frontal cortex correlates with reduced MeCP2 protein. Both genetic and epigenetic routes converge on a partial MeCP2 deficit below the Rett threshold.

evidence.snippet: A significant reduction in MeCP2 expression compared to age-matched controls was found in 11/14 autism (79%)

evidence.reference_title: Reduced MeCP2 expression is frequent in autism frontal cortex and correlates with aberrant MECP2 promoter methylation.
evidence.snippet: A more frequent occurrence was significantly increased MECP2 promoter methylation in autism male frontal cortex compared to controls.

evidence.reference_title: MECP2 coding sequence and 3'UTR variation in 172 unrelated autistic patients.
